figures.title: Effects of canvas resolution and ground-truth mask area
notes: The canvas sets the output resolution, apart from the glimpse's.
A: from a single 128-pixel glimpse of the whole scene, a finer canvas segments better,
and beats its input-matched DINOv3 teacher, whose output is 8 by 8.
Finer canvases help most on small masks: small, distant or occluded objects.
B: finer canvases also gain the most from additional glimpses.
C: accuracy against compute; CanViT-B adds glimpses, DINOv3 adds input pixels.

figures.title: Pretraining ablations
notes: Short pretraining runs, about a tenth of the flagship's compute, each changing one thing; frozen, with linear readouts.
Removing dense supervision costs the most on ADE20K, and it costs ImageNet-1k accuracy too.
Removing canvas reads or backpropagation through time also hurts both.
On ImageNet-1k, the largest drops come from dropping the full-scene rollout and from a ViT-S backbone.
The viewpoint encoding token matters least here; with a 64 by 64 canvas, it adds about a point at long horizons.

figures.title: Canvas updates within and across glimpses
notes: Each glimpse writes to the canvas three times; here, what each write adds, shown with PCA.
Write 0 mirrors the glimpse's 8 by 8 patch grid.
Write 1 begins to follow the objects in the glimpse.
Write 2 extrapolates beyond the glimpse, with sharper object boundaries.
An emergent progression, from local, feature-level content to scene-wide, semantic content.

figures.title: Impact of the pretraining dataset
notes: Is it the 13 million ImageNet-21k scenes?
We pretrained a second CanViT-B on ImageNet-1k alone, with the same compute budget and hyperparameters.
ADE20K drops; ImageNet-1k accuracy rises slightly when frozen and drops slightly when fine-tuned.
With ImageNet-1k alone, CanViT-B is still ahead of every prior active model.
ImageNet-1k pretraining became unstable late, so we kept the best checkpoint before that, at 92% of training.

figures.title: ImageNet-1k accuracy against inference cost
notes: Our efficiency claims are about dense, scene-wide prediction; on ImageNet-1k, other active models are far cheaper.
We measured AdaptiveNN and GFNet ourselves, from their released code and checkpoints, after a fixed number of glimpses.
Fine-tuned, CanViT-B is the most accurate with one glimpse and with a few,
at many times the compute per glimpse.

figures.title: Architecture control
notes: How much of this is DINOv3?
We trained CanViT-B and an AdaGlimpse baseline from scratch with the same DINOv3 teacher, ImageNet-1k images and glimpse budget,
then read out both the same way: frozen, linear, Entropy-Guided Coarse-to-Fine, a 32 by 32 output.
CanViT-B is ahead at every glimpse, by 18 points at the fourth.
Its fourth glimpse costs less compute than the baseline's first,
and it trained in about a tenth of the TPU chip-hours: 22 against 212.
The absolute numbers also reflect the strength of the DINOv3 teacher.

figures.title: COCO object detection
notes: A preliminary experiment: CanViT-B fine-tuned with a CenterNet detection head.
From the architecture control, with identical heads, CanViT-B more than doubles AdaGlimpse's AP at every glimpse.
The flagship, fine-tuned longer with 10 glimpses: AP keeps rising through glimpse 21.
Simple and experimental, but the canvas supports detection.

figures.title: Learned viewing policies
notes: Two standard objectives, Q-learning and REINFORCE, 8 training runs each, on the frozen CanViT-B and its frozen probe.
Both beat Entropy-Guided Coarse-to-Fine from the second glimpse on.
Each run's checkpoint was selected on ADE20K validation, the split reported here; the last checkpoints are within about a tenth of a point.
